title: Server-authoritative amount
description: Order amount, currency and discounts come from the server; mismatches cannot fulfill.
risk: A buyer edits the price or currency in the browser, or pays less than the total, and still receives the goods.
requires: Server catalog/order and provider amount/currency match.

title: Order and merchant binding
description: Payment, merchant, customer and order identities agree before fulfillment.
risk: A payment made for one order is used to fulfill a different one, such as paying for a cheap order to release an expensive one.
requires: Cross-object identity checks plus a business-state oracle.

title: Webhook authenticity
description: Provider signature validation uses the original body and provider-specific verification.
risk: Anyone who finds the webhook URL can forge a "payment succeeded" event and receive goods without paying.
requires: Provider-specific verification plus negative sandbox cases.

title: Verified fulfillment
description: Only a verified successful payment can authorize the matching business action.
risk: Orders are fulfilled on failed, pending or unknown payments, so goods leave without money arriving.
requires: Provider success correlated with committed fulfillment.

title: Object authorization
description: Another account cannot read, capture, refund or fulfill the order.
risk: One customer can read, pay for, refund or fulfill another customer's order.
requires: Two owned synthetic identities and order-level isolation.

title: Idempotency and replay
description: Retries, duplicate events and concurrent delivery cannot duplicate economic effects.
risk: A retried or duplicated event fulfills or refunds the same order more than once.
requires: Repeated/concurrent delivery causes one economic effect.

title: Payment lifecycle
description: Delayed, reordered, failed, refunded and disputed states reconcile correctly.
risk: Late, out-of-order, refunded or disputed events leave the order in the wrong state, such as still fulfilled after a refund.

title: Secret isolation
description: Secret credentials remain server-side, isolated by environment and least privilege.
risk: A leaked secret key lets someone else act as the merchant: create charges, issue refunds or sign fake events.
requires: Source/config review and redacted runtime evidence.

title: Sensitive-data minimization
description: No real card data, credentials or personal identifiers in retained artifacts.
risk: Card data, credentials or personal details end up in logs and traces, where a leak exposes them.

title: Payment-page integrity
description: Scripts and browser protections follow the applicable integration threat model.
risk: A tampered or injected script on the payment page can skim card details or alter the payment.
requires: Scripts, deployment policy and applicable provider guidance.

title: Recovery and reconciliation
description: Dropped events and outages recover without silently losing payment/order consistency.
risk: A dropped event or crashed worker leaves a paid order unfulfilled, and nobody notices.
requires: Dropped event and worker-failure recovery traces.

title: Audit and maintenance
description: Versioned dependencies, redacted traces and alerting support incident response.
risk: Without version history, an audit trail or alerts, an incident cannot be detected or reconstructed.
requires: Version provenance, dependency review and audit events.
